summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man was admitted for evaluation of atypical chest pain and worsening shortness of breath. Initial concern for cardiac ischemia was ruled out with serial troponins and a normal stress MIBI test showing no perfusion defects and preserved ejection fraction. His chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, possibly musculoskeletal. Shortness of breath was attributed to COPD, with oxygen desaturation on exertion, leading to initiation of inhaled bronchodilators and home oxygen therapy. Hypothyroidism was identified with elevated TSH and low free T4, prompting an increase in levothyroxine dose. The patient was monitored for alcohol withdrawal without complications and engaged in plans for outpatient support. He was discharged stable with new prescriptions, follow-up arranged with pulmonology and primary care, and instructions for medication adherence and symptom monitoring.
